MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 9, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on October 9, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 4, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:12 p.m.)
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Sachs declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:04
p.m. with all five City Council Members present

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

City Council Minutes  1  October 9, 2018
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  OCTA Update: OC Flex Program

  Johnny Dunning, OCTA Manager of Scheduling and Operations, highlighted the new
  OCTA Flex program, an on-demand ride service which will be operated as a one-year pilot
  in select areas, including portions of Mission Viejo.

P2.  Recreation Programs and Membership Enhancements

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix, Community Services
  Commissioner Bob Ruesch, and Community Services Manager Lydie Gutfeld presented
  updates on the City's recreation programs, membership enhancements and the new Special
  Needs Adaptive Program (SNAP).

P3.  30th Annual Walk Against Drugs

  Khatra Molina, OCSD Crime Prevention Specialist, announced that the 30th Annual Walk
  Against Drugs will be held on Saturday, October 20, 2018, and she provided details of the
  event.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bill Moorhead, M.V.: introduced himself as a candidate for Director of Moulton Niguel Water
District and asked residents to visit his website (moorheadforwater.com) to learn more about his
positions.

Sherry Wanninger, M.V.: announced that she is a candidate for Moulton Niguel Water District
Board and she said she looks forward to bringing a fresh perspective as the Board meets the
challenges ahead.

Ben Mayer, M.V.: representing the Mission Viejo Community of Character Committee, he
announced that October’s character trait is respect and he outlined various traits that demonstrate
respect.

Melanie Smith, M.V.: introduced Spirit League, the only sports league in Orange County for
people with special needs. She invited the Council and community to watch a “Pack the Bleachers”
soccer game on Saturday, October 13 from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at the Oso fields and a Swing
for Autism event on November 9 in Coto de Caza. In closing, Mrs. Smith thanked the Council for
letting Spirit League be a part of the City’s sports team family.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

City Council Minutes  2  October 9, 2018
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of September 25, 2018, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated September 14, 2018 in the Amount of $1,483,290.16

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated September 21, 2018 in the Amount of $2,464,496.74

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Marguerite Parkway Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP 17230)

  (1) Authorized the conditional removal of the south leg crosswalk on Marguerite Parkway
  at the intersection of Felipe Road/La Mancha pending feedback received during the 30-day
  public comment period; and (2) directed staff to return to City Council following the
  conclusion of said 30-day period with a summary of public comments received and a final
  recommendation regarding the proposed disposition of the crosswalk.

5.  Financial Report for Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2018

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS

6.  Temporarily Exceed the Authorized Position Schedule

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented staff report.

  Mayor Sachs recommended that staff consider drafting a policy that would allow them to
  exceed authorized positions for recruiting purposes, with certain limitations and for defined
  periods of time, without Council approval.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  adopt Resolution 18-42 Authorizing Staff to Temporarily Exceed the Current Authorized
  Position Schedule.

City Council Minutes  3  October 9, 2018
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

7.  Close out of FY 2017/18 and FY 2018/19 Budget Adjustments for Certain Revenue
  and Expenditure Accounts.

  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services, presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 18-43 Amending the FY 2017/18 City Budget for Year-End Close Out
  Adjustments in Certain Accounts and Funds; and (2) adopt Resolution 18-44 Amending
  the FY 2018/19 City Budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

8.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Sachs deferred the report to the next meeting.

9.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

10.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

11.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Sachs announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the TCA Board and he
  will have a report at the next Council meeting.

STAFF REPORTS

12.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update from Chief Vuong

  Chief Vuong announced that OCSD-Mission Viejo will host a School Safety Symposium
  on Thursday, October 11 from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council chamber to solicit feedback
City Council Minutes  4  October 9, 2018
   from the community on ways to make schools safer in the City. He noted that the Safe
  Schools Challenge videos will be posted on social media on Monday October 15 and the
  first traffic assessment public meeting will be held on October 18 at 9:00 a.m. at City Hall
  for members of the public to express traffic concerns. Chief Vuong announced that OCSD
  Professional Services Responders will begin helping with the citizen patrol program for
  additional patrol checks, limited parking enforcement, fire watch, and crime prevention
  support efforts. He noted that the Adopt-A-Cop program is expanding to Linda Vista, Glen
  Yermo and Del Lago schools and OCSD-Mission Viejo received two new electronic
  bicycles that can go up to 50 mph and will help deputies patrol the City. Chief Vuong
  shared that the City’s homeless liaison officer was able to help a man who has been
  homeless for 13 years find permanent housing through Family Assistance Ministries.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum discussed her attendance at the "topping” ceremony for the new cancer
center near Mission Hospital. Attendees signed the beam before it was placed on top of the building
and she thanked staff and Mission Hospital for helping to bring the facility to town. Council
Member Bucknum announced that she enjoyed the 6th annual Mission Armed Forces football
game, especially when witnessing the pride on the faces of the veterans who were honored. She
said it was great to see the patriotism of the students, parents and even the opposing team. Council
Member Bucknum reviewed upcoming events including the 8th annual Tee It Up Fore Marines
golf tournament on October 12, the 30th annual Walk Against Drugs on October 20, and Pumpkin
Diving on October 21, 2018.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she recently traveled to Washington, DC to attend the
National Forum on Character with Library and Cultural Services Coordinator Vickie Sullivan. She
said it was an honor to present a breakout session on Mission Viejo’s Community of Character
program and the session was extremely well received. Council Member Kelley noted that it is
common to find character programs in schools across the nation but it is rare to find a City of
Character that focuses on character qualities and provides materials to every school in town. She
discussed the character word for the month, respect, and displayed the materials that are available
at the schools each month and on the City's website at https://cityofmissionviejo.org/character.
Council Member Kelley announced that this month’s character movie is Wonder and it will be
shown on Sunday, October 28 at 2:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber.

City Council Minutes  5  October 9, 2018
 Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell echoed Council Member Bucknum’s comments and said it was great to
see the beam lifted in the air and placed on top of the new cancer center building. He noted that
people had signed the beam and the contractor’s tradition is to lay an American Flag on the beam
for the ceremony, along with a tree that will be planted nearby. He said the cancer treatment center
will bring new opportunities for Mission Viejo residents and all those in South County. Council
Member Goodell stated that he is looking forward to the Tee it Up Fore Marines golf tournament
and the Red Ribbon Walk next week. He also discussed recent meetings with experts in the real
estate industry who are bringing fresh ideas for updating and transforming some of the shopping
centers in town.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked members of the Knights of Columbus from St. Kilian’s Catholic
Church for attending the Council meeting tonight and a member of the Elks Lodge who attends
monthly to report back to the organization. He said the Elks held a breakfast fundraiser last week
for local veterans that was very successful. Mayor Pro Tem Raths also recognized the Rotary Club
and noted that they meet weekly on Thursday mornings from 7:10 a.m. to 8:30 a.m. and a different
guest speaker is featured each week. He expressed appreciation to the Orange County Sheriff’s
Department for all they do and he thanked retiring Sheriff Sandra Hutchens for her support of
Mission Viejo. Mayor Pro Tem Raths said he looks forward to Friday’s Marine benefit golf
tournament and in closing, he gave a shout out to Casta del Sol resident and City liaison Carole
Weidler and said he hopes she didn't miss tonight’s meeting because she is sick.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs discussed the Mission Viejo High School salute to veterans’ football game where
100 vets were recognized with the football players wearing the veterans’ names on the backs of
their jerseys. He said he was honored to have his name on the back of “TJ’s” jersey and it was
terrific meeting the young man before he went out to play the football game. Afterward, all the
vets walked out onto the field with their representative football players and he said it was an all-
around great evening. Mayor Sachs discussed his meeting earlier in the day with a company that
helps solar customers manage their solar usage and billing. He also shared that utility companies
are going to be shifting the prime time for use of power from the current 10:00 or 11:00 a.m. to
6:00 p.m., to a new block from 4:00 p.m. to 9:30 p.m., and looking at new tiers to try and make up
for some of their loss due to solar. He recommended that Chief Capobianco share the information
with Orange County Fire Authority and noted that the program doesn’t cost anything because it is
subsidized by the utility companies. Mayor Sachs said he discussed the program with the City
Manager and he looks forward to setting up a meeting with staff to explore it more. Discussing the
Tee it Up Fore Marines golf tournament, Mayor Sachs announced that the Mission Viejo Country
Club is sending 40 players to make up 10 teams and he thanked John Petke for working so hard to
put the teams together. He shared that earlier today he saw three more cars run a left turn on red
light signal and he suggested that the striping on Oso Parkway, leading to the northbound ramp to
the 5 freeway, be clarified to reduce the clogging that occurs when people who are going
southbound line up in the wrong lane.

City Council Minutes  6  October 9, 2018
 City Manager Wilberg said that staff is working with Caltrans to have it corrected and there have
been some ongoing frustrations with that project and others.

Chief Capobianco responded to a question about fire station open houses and noted that the OCFA
headquarters tour was last Saturday and Mission Viejo Station 24 will host its open house this
coming Saturday, October 13, 2018, from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:06 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, October 23, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 23, 2018

City Council Minutes  7  October 9, 2018
